visual: Dense carpet of trailing stems in rounded gold-green leaves · small yellow cups
water: Never let it dry out · thrives in wet ground
soilWarning: Roots as it runs · will swamp small plants
prune: Cut back the running stems whenever it outgrows its patch
hardinessNote: Hardy throughout the UK and northern Europe, approximately -20 to -15°C.
resilience: Very hardy and vigorous · establishes fast wherever it stays damp
uses: Ground cover · pond margins and bog gardens · banks · trailing from pots
uncertain: peak: supplied research said "Summer"; converted to Jun-Aug so the app can parse it. Not from a source that stated months.

latin: the supplied JSON put the cultivar in cvs and left latin as the bare species. The plain species is the green creeping Jenny; the photograph and the common name are the golden one, so 'Aurea' was moved into latin the way the rest of the deck carries its cultivars.

compliance: left blank, not researched here. Creeping Jenny is a known vigorous spreader (the card says so in its soil warning) and is listed as invasive in parts of North America; whether any UK statutory duty applies was NOT verified, and blank means nothing is known to apply rather than nothing does.
